page: Vultr voc-s-16c-128gb-2560s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features an AMD EPYC processor with 16 shared vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with multi-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled locally, consisting of a 2560 GB NVMe SSD. No GPU hardware is present.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong memory capabilities and solid compute throughput. The instance achieves top-tier status in large-block memory write bandwidth, reaching 170.21 GB/sec, and strong performance in large-block read-only memory bandwidth at 339.94 GB/sec. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25%, while multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores align with average mid-tier expectations. Cryptographic and vector operations are supported via hardware-accelerated AES, SHA_NI, and AVX instructions.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a dense resource profile, combining high-capacity memory and substantial NVMe storage on shared CPU resources. The shared CPU allocation represents a potential tradeoff, as compute performance may experience variability compared to dedicated core instances. However, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and fast local storage make it a resource-dense option for workloads that are memory-bound rather than continuously compute-intensive.

This hardware profile is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, and caching layers such as Redis, where it achieves an average of 36.59 million operations per second. It is also appropriate for medium-scale web serving, data processing, and lightweight language model inference, demonstrating average performance on 7B parameter models.
